understanding: The supplied code shows a Raft library with caller-selected FSM, log, stable-storage, snapshot and transport interfaces. Local understanding is partial: command submission, commitment bookkeeping, FSM callbacks, snapshot capture, snapshot orchestration, file-sink closure and log compaction are visible. Replication acknowledgements, configuration activation, startup restoration and several asynchronous consumers remain unread. Interface comments describe intended guarantees separately from the observed implementation. The inventory below records local assertions without treating enqueueing as commitment, callback return as durable application, or repeated sink Close success as proof of publication. No correctness, calibration or reproduction conclusion is established.

target_profile.system_boundary: The raft package, including its orchestration and in-repository adapter implementations. Application FSM internals and separately maintained storage backends are outside the supplied implementation evidence. Caller injection does not exclude built-in implementations from this inventory.
protocol_contexts: Raft instances maintain local identity, current term, role, indexed logs and configuration state.
RPC processing checks supported protocol versions and compatibility with the configured speaking version.
A commitment object is documented as belonging to one leader tenure; actual construction and retirement call sites remain unread.
FSM processing and snapshot orchestration execute in separate background workers started by NewRaft.
external_interfaces: NewRaft accepts Config, FSM, LogStore, StableStore, SnapshotStore and Transport.
Apply and ApplyLog return ApplyFuture objects; Barrier and VerifyLeader return Future objects.
FSM exposes Apply, Snapshot and Restore; BatchingFSM optionally exposes ApplyBatch.
FSMSnapshot exposes Persist and Release, with a caller-provided SnapshotSink.
Transport exposes RPC delivery, replication, voting, snapshot transfer, heartbeat handling and leadership-transfer requests; WithPreVote is optional.
ownership: NewRaft initializes shared state and starts run, runFSM and runSnapshots unless skipStartup is set.
runFSM owns the local lastIndex and lastTerm used in snapshot-capture responses.
takeSnapshot obtains configuration state through a future because that state is owned by the main thread.
commitment serializes match-index and commit-index access with a mutex.
Transport may invoke the registered heartbeat handler concurrently with blocking RPC processing.
Application clients implement FSM callbacks; their internal state and persistence are not supplied.
selection_injection: NewRaft stores caller-provided storage, transport and FSM implementations directly.
Pre-vote is disabled when configured off or when the supplied transport does not implement WithPreVote.
BatchApplyCh selects buffered versus unbuffered command admission; this is separate from the BatchingFSM type assertion.
runFSM selects batch application and configuration callbacks through BatchingFSM and ConfigurationStore type assertions.
FileSnapshotSink is a concrete built-in implementation observed here; whether any actual deployment selects it is unknown.
The file catalogue also lists in-memory, discard-snapshot, log-cache and network transport implementations; their semantics and activation remain unread.
variants: Protocol-version compatibility affects accepted RPC headers and permitted server identity/address relationships.
Candidate campaigns may use pre-vote, direct election or a leadership-transfer path that bypasses pre-vote.
Single-entry and batch FSM application use different filtering and progress-update paths.
File snapshot closure conditionally synchronizes files and, outside Windows, the parent directory according to noSync.
Startup restoration and runtime FSM restoration are distinct paths.
unknowns: No concrete deployment configuration or selected storage/transport instance is supplied.
LogStore and StableStore failure and durability contracts, including built-in implementations, remain unread.
Leader dispatch, follower append processing and replication-result producers have not been inspected.
Election helper implementations, term persistence and role-transition side effects remain unresolved callees.
Snapshot metadata writing, enumeration, opening, retention and constructor options require inspection.
Package-test capability is reported by the framework, but no test observations are supplied here; precise schedule replay is unavailable.
